label: input token f at original position >= 4
explanation: Fires when the input token is the letter f during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position t >= 4. It is silent on f at positions 0-3, on any other input token, and on the delimiter and copy phases. That includes f being fed back or output during the copy phase. Magnitude rises steeply with position: computed from the profile, mean activation is about 0.28 at t=4, 1.2 at t=5, 1.9 at t=6, 2.4 at t=7 and 2.6 at t=8. The top examples are all f at t=8 in L=9 sequences. It is roughly independent of preceding tokens, first token, digits and repeat counts. Dev F1 is 0.9998. The few misses are tiny activations (<0.03 of max) at t=8 on other tokens.

issues: Minor rounding: the explanation says test precision, recall, F1 and mass recall are all 1.000. The actual test scores are precision 1.0, recall 0.99971, F1 0.99986 and mass recall 0.99999. The 12 missed test steps are all at t=8, on non-f tokens, at 0.01-0.02 of max, and carry 0.0% of the activation mass. That is scattered noise, not a systematic class.

The rest checks out. There are no test false positives. f at t<4 scores precision 0 against 66,339 predicted steps, so it is silent there. Delimiter and copy phases have 0 active steps. Activity is confined to t=4..8, with a firing rate of about 0.033 at every orig_idx 4..8, which matches the frequency of f. Mean magnitudes derived from mass share are 0.28, 1.22, 1.94, 2.41 and 2.62 for t=4..8, matching the stated profile. Firing rates by prev_tok and prev2_tok are flat.
